mechanics.name: Adrenaline
mechanics.currentEffect: When the Exit Gates are powered, heal one Health State if you are injured or in the Dying State, then gain 50% Haste for 4 seconds. Adrenaline can activate while Exhausted and ignores the existing Exhausted timer; afterward it applies Exhausted for 60/50/40 seconds by tier. It does not activate if you are hooked or being carried when the Exit Gates are powered.
activation: You must not be hooked or being carried at that moment.
If injured or downed, the heal restores one Health State.
The perk can activate while you are already Exhausted.
mechanics.patchNote: 10.1.0 increased Haste duration to 4 seconds. It does not activate if you are hooked or carried when the gates are powered.

editorial.summary: When the Exit Gates are powered, recover one Health State if eligible and gain 50% Haste for 4 seconds.
useCases: Turn the final generator into an instant reset and chase extension.
Recover from the Dying State as the gates power.
Coordinate the final generator around a teammate currently in chase.
counters: Provides no value if the team never powers the gates.
Broken can prevent the healing component.
Being hooked or carried at gate power prevents activation.
pros: Combines healing and mobility in one instant trigger.
Exceptionally strong when the last generator is deliberately timed.
cons: Entire perk slot is dormant until endgame.
Solo Q cannot always control when the final generator pops.
Hooked or carried Survivors miss the activation.
analysis: Adrenaline is the definition of delayed power. For most of the Trial it does nothing, but when the gates are powered it can instantly erase a health-state deficit and create four seconds of 50% Haste. That combination can convert a losing endgame chase into an escape or turn a slug into a Survivor who is suddenly standing and moving at high speed.

Its 10.1.0 buff to four seconds of Haste matters because endgame positions are often decided by a few metres. The extra second increases the odds of reaching a gate, strong tile, or teammate protection before the Killer can capitalize on the final generator completing.

The Solo Q weakness is timing control. A random teammate may finish the last generator while you are hooked, being carried, or seconds away from a safer activation. In SWF, that weakness almost disappears because the team can 99% the final gen, communicate the chase state, and trigger Adrenaline at the exact moment it creates maximum value.

Adrenaline also pairs naturally with Sprint Burst because it ignores an existing Exhausted timer when it activates. Meg therefore offers two top-five perks that cover opposite halves of the match: Sprint Burst for repeated positioning and Adrenaline for the decisive endgame swing.
editorial.verdict: One of the strongest endgame perks available. It asks you to carry a dormant slot for most of the match, then repays that investment with a potentially match-winning heal and speed burst.
